summary: Package beacons installer host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and require time
details: The package ships no real functionality: index.js (declared main) exports a Proxy whose every property returns a no-op, and the package's advertised purpose is a generic 'compatibility shim'. The actual payload is beacon.cjs. A postinstall hook ("node beacon.cjs") runs the beacon on npm install, and index.js re-fires the same beacon on require(). The beacon collects host identifiers — os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), process.version, and the package name — and POSTs them in plaintext HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The combination of a hardcoded bare-IP plaintext C2, install-time and require-time auto-execution, host identifier collection, and a no-op facade in place of real functionality is the fingerprint of a reconnaissance / name-squat beacon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
